about: QA corrections from the live windows_nodata runs of 23 Oct 2026 (Cerebras judge), parsed from each run's qa_N.json, with the item as the Researcher wrote it. kb_verdict = Claude's check against the KB; expect = the KB shield's intended result (Step 7.6g). Gap source_ids were added as the new prompt asks.

item.text: No official source confirms which UAE ministry is the issuing authority for the India CEPA certificate.

correction.problem: Incorrect claim that no official source confirms the issuing ministry.
correction.fix: Official source P-MOET-COO-INDIA confirms the Ministry of Foreign Trade issues the CEPA certificate for India.

cases.why: fix says P-MOET-COO-INDIA confirms MoFT issues the certificate; P-UAE-ISSUER's note says no official page names MoFT (problem 82)

cases.item: Confirm which UAE ministry issues the CEPA certificate for India (the Ministry of Foreign Trade or the Ministry of Economy and Tourism).

correction.problem: Question about which UAE ministry issues the CEPA certificate does not affect origin qualification.
correction.fix: Remove this question as it does not impact the origin determination.

cases.why: asking the user which ministry issues the certificate cannot change the origin result

item.text: The agreement does not define 'direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' needed for the build-up value addition method.

correction.problem: The claim that the agreement does not define 'direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' is unsupported.
correction.fix: The agreement specifies the rule 'CTSH + VA 45%' but does not define the components of CTSH such as direct labour cost or direct overhead cost.

cases.why: fix ties direct labour/overhead cost to CTSH; it keeps 'does not define', so the shield cannot see it (known limit)

item.text: The agreement does not state whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold for value addition.

correction.problem: The statement about the agreement not stating whether build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold is unsupported.
correction.fix: The cited records do not provide information on whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold for value addition.

cases.why: the gap is P-AGR-3.2.2-VA's own note; the fix drops 'does not state' (harmless wording, but a false rejection)

item.text: The factory registration requires a 40% domestic value added letter, but the CEPA product-specific rule requires 45% value addition; the relationship is unclear.

correction.problem: The claim that the relationship between the 40% domestic value added letter and the 45% rule is unclear contradicts the record, which clarifies they are separate.
correction.fix: The factory registration requires a 40% domestic value added letter, while the CEPA product-specific rule requires 45% value addition; the registration requirement is separate and does not serve as the rule of origin test.

cases.why: P-MOET-FACTORY-REG says the 40% letter is a registration condition, not the PSR test; the gap called it unclear

item.note: Direct labour cost and direct overhead cost are not defined in the agreement, so the build-up value addition method is uncertain.

correction.problem: The note adds an unsupported inference that the build-up value addition method is uncertain.
correction.fix: Direct labour cost and direct overhead cost are not defined in the agreement.

cases.why: the note added 'so the build-up method is uncertain', which the record does not say

item.text: The agreement does not define 'direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' for the build-up value addition method.

correction.problem: The claim about the agreement not defining 'direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' is not supported by any cited record.
correction.fix: The cited records do not provide information on whether the agreement defines 'direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' for the build‑up value addition method.

cases.why: the gap is P-AGR-3.2.2-VA's note almost word for word (problem 81)

item.text: No official source confirms that the Ministry of Foreign Trade is the issuing authority for the India CEPA certificate; India's origin rules list the Ministry of Economy or any other agency notified.

correction.problem: The statement contradicts the cited record that identifies the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuing authority.
correction.fix: The Ministry of Foreign Trade is identified as the issuing authority for the India CEPA Certificate of Origin in the cited records.

cases.why: fix says MoFT is identified as the issuer; P-UAE-ISSUER's note says the opposite; the writer copied it (problem 82)

item.text: No official confirmation is available that a free-zone factory cannot obtain Factory Registration, which is a prerequisite for the certificate of origin.

correction.problem: The claim contradicts the cited record which confirms that free‑zone factories cannot obtain registration.
correction.fix: According to the cited record, factory registration requires the factory to be located outside a free zone, confirming that free‑zone factories cannot obtain registration.

cases.why: the KB marks it 'Inference ... likely ... confirm'; the fix turns it into a confirmed fact

item.note: Value addition percentages are on an FOB basis; on an Ex-Works basis the threshold is 5 percentage points lower.

correction.problem: The note adds that value addition percentages are on an FOB basis, which is not stated in the cited record.
correction.fix: The value addition threshold is 5 percentage points lower when the Ex-Works price is used as the basis.

cases.why: 'FOB basis' is in P-AGR-3.2.2-VA, not in the cited PSR-GEN-EXW (wrong citation)

item.note: The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge, and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.

correction.problem: The note claims CEPA reduces only Basic Customs Duty, omitting the reduction of Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess and incorrectly using "only".
correction.fix: The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty and, for lines in Table II, also the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge, and any anti‑dumping or safeguard duty still apply.

cases.why: the agricultural cess applies to Table II lines only; 7610 10 00 is not one

item.note: The duty saving is estimated on BCD only; the actual saving depends on the shipment value and other duties.

correction.problem: The note adds that duty saving depends on shipment value, which is not stated in the cited record.
correction.fix: CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty only; no shipment value was provided, so only the rate difference is shown.

cases.why: no saving was estimated (NEEDS_VALUE); the note said 'estimated'

item.note: 'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' in the value-addition build-up method are not defined in the agreement.

correction.problem: The claim about undefined "Direct labour cost" and "direct overhead cost" is not supported by any cited record.
correction.fix: Remove this note or replace it with information that is supported by the available evidence.

cases.why: the fact is in the KB, but the cited ID P-AGR-3.2-VA does not exist (code already flags it)

item.note: The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty and, for lines in Table II, also the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge, and any anti‑dumping or safeguard duty still apply.

correction.problem: The note omits the 'countervailing' duty qualifier present in the source record.
correction.fix: The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty and, for lines in Table II, also the Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge, and any anti‑dumping, countervailing or safeguard duties still apply.

cases.why: right about the record ('countervailing'), but the gap came from QA's own round-1 wording
